The rule streams of the mortality triage

Source: R/mortality_rules.R
mortality_rules.Rd

Returns the default rule streams as a list that detect_mortality() runs in order. Each stream is a small function of the detection set that returns, per animal, a vote, a score, a candidate date and the rows behind them. The streams sort animals for a person to review; they never make the call. Add a stream with mortality_rule(), drop one with drop, or change a setting by name. Each setting is given with its default.

Usage

mortality_rules(..., drop = character())

Arguments

...

Settings to change, by name, such as min_days = 21 or accel_flat = 0.05. A name sets that setting in every stream that has it; a name no stream has is an error. The options sites_km, site_distance and sparse_to_review of detect_mortality()'s control may be given here too; they travel with the rules, and control overrides them.

drop

Names of default streams to leave out.

Value

A named list of class mortality_rules, one mortality_rule per stream, in the order they run.

Details

  • accel_flatline (votes dead or alive). A day is flat when the 95th percentile of its calibrated acceleration is at or below accel_flat (0.10 m/s2). The stream votes dead when at least min_flat_days (14) observed days are flat from the last active day to the end of the sensor record, and alive when a day within active_within_days (30) of the last detection is active. A day needs min_readings (1) readings, and an active spell min_active_days (1) days. Raw readings are converted with the transmitter's sensor_slope and sensor_intercept; without them the stream cannot vote. The candidate date is the day after the last active day.

  • terminal_run (votes dead, or review). Stations are clustered into sites (see control in detect_mortality()). The final window holds the last min_days (14) detection days and at least the last min_calendar_days (14) calendar days. The stream votes dead when every detection in the window falls in one site and the bounding-box diagonal of its stations is at most the site size. It votes review when the window spans more than one site but its stations lie within the site size of each other; when one station heard it all and the station's recorded position moved; when its stations lie within near_factor (2) times the site size; or when every window day but at most stray_days (2) is at one site. The candidate date is the first detection of the final run, the stray days aside.

  • depth_flatline (evidence only). A day is flat when its depth range is at most depth_flat (0.3 m), or depth_flat_share (0.1) of the day's median depth when that is smaller. It votes dead after min_flat_days (14) flat days to the end of the sensor record, and never decides a band. A day needs min_readings (1) readings.

Sensor resolution. A sensor reports whole counts, so a dead tag whose reading moves one count either side of its resting value spans two counts in a day. Both flatline streams therefore never set a flat limit below two counts of the sensor: the limit is the larger of the limit above and two counts. A count is the transmitter's sensor_slope in the animals table, on the calibrated scale; the example's depth tags have 0.1504 m per count, so two counts are 0.3008 m and a day of one-count noise reads flat. Where the readings arrive calibrated with no slope, a count is the smallest gap between two distinct calibrated values of that transmitter; readings that are not whole counts give a small gap, which leaves the limit as set. At a resolution as coarse as the example's, two counts exceed the shallow-water share of the median depth, so the share narrows no limit below 0.3008 m. Values are compared with a floating-point tolerance.

  • record_end (censors). Votes review when the last detection falls within within_days (30) of the expected end: the earliest of the tag's life from release, the data horizon and the end of the detection record (control$horizon in detect_mortality()). Its detail on the card names which end applied and why: a record heard to the end of the detection record is cut off there, its end unknown, so the rules cannot see what followed.

  • site_listening (evidence; votes review when switched on). Counts the days, of the within_days (30) after the last detection, on which a receiver at the site of the last detection was listening. When listening_share (0) is above 0 and the site listened on a smaller share of those days, it votes review. At the default it is evidence for the cards only.

  • movement_resumption (votes alive). After the earliest candidate death date of the streams before it, a transmitter heard on at least min_days_away (2) days at stations more than the site size from every station that heard it on its first ref_days (3) detection days from that date has moved, and the stream votes alive.

  • persistence (ranks). The trailing-core Jaccard score. For each day, the core is the set of stations that logged coverage (0.95) of the animal's detections in the previous window_days (30); the score is the mean Jaccard similarity between cores lag_days (7) apart, from 0 to 1. A record needs min_record_days (45) detection days, windows need min_window_days (10), and the mean needs min_pairs (20) pairs. The score orders the review band. A score of at least review_at (0.95) sends an animal with no other evidence to review; review_at = Inf ranks only.

Sources. The kinds of evidence the streams read are those Klinard and Matley (2020, Table 1) found in use across acoustic telemetry studies: a stop in detections, stationary horizontal space use, stationary depth use and stationary acceleration. The streams themselves, their thresholds and defaults, the site clustering, the candidate date and the persistence score are this package's own rules. They follow no single published method, which is why a person makes the call on the cards.

References

Klinard, N. V., and Matley, J. K. (2020). Living until proven dead: addressing mortality in acoustic telemetry research. Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries 30, 485-499. doi:10.1007/s11160-020-09613-z

See also

mortality_rule(), detect_mortality()

Examples

mortality_rules()
#> <mortality_rules> 7 streams, run in this order:
#>   accel_flatline       vote     accel_flat = 0.1; min_flat_days = 14;
#>                                 active_within_days = 30; min_readings = 1;
#>                                 min_active_days = 1
#>   terminal_run         vote     min_days = 14; min_calendar_days = 14;
#>                                 near_factor = 2; stray_days = 2
#>   depth_flatline       evidence depth_flat = 0.3; depth_flat_share = 0.1;
#>                                 min_flat_days = 14; min_readings = 1
#>   record_end           censor   within_days = 30
#>   site_listening       vote     within_days = 30; listening_share = 0
#>   movement_resumption  vote     ref_days = 3; min_days_away = 2
#>   persistence          rank     window_days = 30; lag_days = 7; coverage =
#>                                 0.95; min_record_days = 45; min_pairs = 20;
#>                                 min_window_days = 10; review_at = 0.95
mortality_rules(min_days = 21, drop = "persistence")
#> <mortality_rules> 6 streams, run in this order:
#>   accel_flatline       vote     accel_flat = 0.1; min_flat_days = 14;
#>                                 active_within_days = 30; min_readings = 1;
#>                                 min_active_days = 1
#>   terminal_run         vote     min_days = 21; min_calendar_days = 14;
#>                                 near_factor = 2; stray_days = 2
#>   depth_flatline       evidence depth_flat = 0.3; depth_flat_share = 0.1;
#>                                 min_flat_days = 14; min_readings = 1
#>   record_end           censor   within_days = 30
#>   site_listening       vote     within_days = 30; listening_share = 0
#>   movement_resumption  vote     ref_days = 3; min_days_away = 2
